text:
GENERATE BURST KS-Y-steel — Run C-9 P4, ONE steel repaint for the whole sheet (Matt R-C9-22). task_id "KS-Y-steel".

Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1: a sheet of 4 slots holding the SAME knight facing away (N), away to the upper-right (NE), screen-right (E) and the lower-right (SE). His plate armour is painted too PALE, flat and uniformly SPECKLED. Repaint ONLY THE STEEL of all four figures, identically, in the painter's hand shown in IMAGE 2 (the same knight earlier in the process, from a c. 1530 Flemish manuscript): deep, dark gouache modelling on the plate — strong darks in the recesses and under each plate edge, bright highlights on the curves, cool blue-grey and warm grey mixed, a confident dark contour, and small IRREGULAR marks and imperfections (NOT an even speckle). Apply the SAME treatment to every figure so they stay a matched set.
Keep EVERYTHING ELSE EXACTLY as it is: every figure's pose, direction, outline and proportions; the helm SHAPE (rounded skull, smooth rounded visor with one row of holes — only its steel is repainted); the knee wings and plate shapes; the blue tabard, gold heraldry, side flaps and red lining (untouched); the pollaxe; positions on the sheet; flat pure #00ff00 background. For this step the REGISTER CARD above is satisfied BY THE IMAGES: this is a steel repaint, not a restyle.

Two image_gen EDIT calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if any figure's pose/direction/outline/helm shape/tabard changed, the steel is still pale and evenly speckled, the figures no longer match each other, or the background is not flat green — name the reason. Copy outputs to out/KS-Y-steel_a.png and out/KS-Y-steel_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "KS-Y-steel"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — THE SHEET TO EDIT (repaint only the steel, identically on all four)
IMAGE 2 — the painter's hand for the steel (dark gouache modelling, irregular marks)
